The seal of identification and collection includes "three editions of Baoji", "Shiqu Baoji Collection", "Xuantuo honored relatives' treasure", and "Ministry of Education seal of inspection ".　　This work was written by Xuan Ye with one of his own five lines, entitled "Zhao Beikou", which is contained in "The First Collection of Poems of the Qing Shengzu Imperial System", Volume 7. Zhao Beikou is located in Zhili (now in Hebei) 50 miles north of Renqiu County, also known as Tang Xingkou, Zhao Fort mouth, for the confluence of the water of the precipitation. Old embankment, bridge, through the north and south orifice, the bridge is entitled "Yan South Zhao North". Kangxi Emperor had in the middle of spring (February in the lunar calendar) here to read the water around. He went out to the north of the mouth of Zhao to see the ancient town of Yannan a peaceful scene, so the emotion, endowed with this poem for the record. The calligraphy of this poem is well-developed and smooth, with full of ink and brushwork.　　Aisin Gioro Xuan Ye (1654-1722) was the third son of Emperor Shunzhi, the third son of Emperor Kangxi, the Holy Father of the Qing Dynasty. He received a systematic and rigorous initiation into Chinese culture from an early age and had a strong sense of identification with traditional Chinese culture. He was not only a strong advocate of Chinese culture, but also a well-read poet and a keen student, learning calligraphy being one of his important lessons. In his spare time, he often observed the ink of the ancients with his ministers, and exchanged calligraphy skills to cultivate his feelings with ink. Among the calligraphers of all generations, Xuan Ye was the most reverent of Dong Qichang's calligraphy, deliberately imitating it, and eventually becoming an outstanding calligrapher of the Dong School, and directly influencing and leading the direction of the calligraphic style of the time, making the early Qing dynasty calligraphy world pervaded by the residual rhythm of the Dong School.　　This work was once recorded in "Shiqu Baoji Sanshu", and was also verified by the Ministry of Education of the Republic of China, and has been treasured for nearly three hundred years.
